## Introduction

`hySpc.hpc` provides High-Performance Computing (HPC) acceleration routines for the `r-hyperspec` suite. By bridging R with native Rust via `extendr`, `hySpc.hpc` accelerates spatial-spectral operations on large hyperspectral datacubes using sparse iterative Krylov solvers (Conjugate Gradient, BiCGSTAB) and multi-threaded parallel execution (`rayon`).

This guide walks through installation, basic spatial smoothing, thread pool management, and solver configuration.

---

## Installation

Install the development version of `hySpc.hpc` from the `r-hyperspec` repository or GitHub:

```r
# Recommended: Install from r-hyperspec repository
repos <- c("https://r-hyperspec.github.io/pkg-repo/", getOption("repos"))
install.packages("hySpc.hpc", repos = repos)

# Alternatively, install via remotes:
# remotes::install_github("r-hyperspec/hySpc.hpc")
```

---

## 1. Basic Spatial Smoothing with `graphSmooth()`

The central entry point in `hySpc.hpc` is `graphSmooth()`, which applies spatial graph Laplacian smoothing $(I + \alpha L) x = b$ across wavelength channels.

```r
library(hyperSpec)
library(hySpc.hpc)

# Load example hyperspectral dataset (or generate mock spatial data)
set.seed(42)
width <- 50
height <- 50
n_wl <- 100

# Create synthetic noisy spatial-spectral matrix (2500 pixels x 100 wavelengths)
raw_spc <- matrix(rnorm(width * height * n_wl, mean = 50, sd = 10), nrow = width * height, ncol = n_wl)
spc_obj <- new("hyperSpec", spc = raw_spc, wavelength = seq(400, 800, length.out = n_wl))

# Apply 8-neighbor spatial graph smoothing using the native Rust Conjugate Gradient solver
spc_smoothed <- graphSmooth(
  spc_obj, 
  width = width, 
  height = height, 
  alpha = 1.5, 
  neighbors = 8, 
  solver = "cg"
)
```

---

## 2. Choosing the Right Solver Backend

`hySpc.hpc` supports multiple solver backends depending on problem scale and symmetry:

| Solver Option (`solver=`) | Underlying Engine | Best Use Case |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `"cg"` **(Default)** | Native Rust Conjugate Gradient (`csc_matvec`) | Symmetric positive-definite Laplacians (Fastest & memory-efficient) |
| `"bicgstab"` | Native Rust BiCGSTAB (`csc_matvec`) | Asymmetric or directed spatial graph systems |
| `"faer"` | Rust `faer` Sparse Cholesky | Direct sparse matrix factorizations |
| `"dense"` | Base R / LAPACK | Baseline verification on small matrices |

```r
# Example: Using BiCGSTAB solver for directed or weighted graphs
spc_bicg <- graphSmooth(spc_obj, width = width, height = height, alpha = 2.0, solver = "bicgstab")
```

---

## 3. HPC Thread Pool Management

To prevent node over-subscription on shared multi-tenant clusters or Slurm environments, `hySpc.hpc` auto-detects CPU quotas and configures the native `rayon` thread pool:

```r
# Inspect auto-detected CPU quota from Slurm / cgroup / system environment
quota <- get_hpc_thread_limit()
cat("Auto-detected CPU thread limit:", quota, "\n")

# Manually set Rayon worker threads
set_hpc_threads(4)
```
